Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment A mixed day with light to moderate east-southeasterly flow. Rainbow Ridge offers excellent ridge soaring and the strongest thermals; McClellan and Slide Mountain provide dependable sledder/thermic flights. Several sites are hampered by off-direction winds or strong gusts, making prudent site selection essential. The best conditions are late morning through mid-afternoon.

Site Breakdown

  • Kingsbury grade: Marginal — wind direction remains well outside the preferred SE ridge window, providing no ridge lift. Light winds allow sled rides in weak thermals. Preferred window 8am–2pm, peak w* 293 fpm, thermal ceiling ~1500 ft AGL.
  • Hallelujah: Unfavorable — strong easterly winds up to 19 mph are cross/off for the W/SW launches, creating likely lee-side rotor and no usable ridge lift. Even evening drainage winds remain easterly. Not flyable.
  • Slide Mountain: Favorable — wind direction within the wide preferred range (SE–S), light 2–6 mph. Good thermals for sledders, peak w* 254 fpm, ceiling ~1000 ft AGL. Window 9am–3pm.
  • McClellan: Favorable — light variable winds, mostly in-range, with strong thermals (peak 354 fpm) and a decent ceiling ~1900 ft AGL. Prime thermal window 10am–5pm, best after 12:30pm.
  • West McClellan: Marginal — wind direction off for ridge soaring (ESE–SE rather than WSW–WNW). Light winds permit thermal-only flying with peak w* 273 fpm, ceiling ~1700 ft AGL. Window 11am–4pm.
  • Peavine Mountain: Marginal — moderate SE winds 10–15 mph (lighter 11am–3pm) can feel strong, and thermal ceiling is very low (~600 ft AGL). Peak w* 229 fpm; only short sled hops possible. Window 11am–3pm.
  • Rainbow Ridge: Favorable — ideal ENE winds 9–11 mph squarely within the preferred range. Combined with robust thermals (peak w* 361 fpm), a 2300 ft AGL ceiling, and zero cloud. The top site of the day. Window 9am–5pm. Note hazardous low-level speed shear of 6 mph at 240 ft AGL; pilots should maintain airspeed margin.
  • Duck Hill: Marginal — wind direction from S–SE is off for the NW/N launches, negating ridge lift. Thermals are good (peak 321 fpm, ceiling ~2300 ft AGL) in light winds, making sledder flights viable. Window 10am–5pm.
  • Daydreams: Marginal — morning brings strong cross/off wind 21–22 mph, likely lee turbulence. Afternoon winds drop to 2–5 mph (still off-direction), allowing cautious sled flights. Peak w* 274 fpm, thermal ceiling ~1350 ft AGL. Overdevelopment clouds 18% of the time; preferred afternoon window 2pm–5pm.

Hazards

  • Rotor/lee turbulence: Strong easterly flow at Hallelujah (19 mph) and Daydreams (22 mph) will generate significant lee-side turbulence downwind of the Carson Range and local ridges.
  • Low-level wind shear: Layer speed shear reaches hazardous thresholds at Rainbow Ridge (6 mph at 240 ft AGL) and Hallelujah (5 mph at 762 ft AGL). Pilots ridge-soaring these sites should expect sudden shear.
  • Overdevelopment: Cloud bases encroach into the thermal zone at Daydreams (18% of flying hours) and Kingsbury (14%), increasing the risk of unwanted cloud encounters in thermals.

Site Forecast ?Top of Thermals (PBLH) — height of the turbulent mixing layer; thermals typically reach this ceiling.
LCL (Lifted Condensation Level) — altitude where rising air reaches its dew point; theoretical cloud base.
Cloud Base — lowest model level with >10% cloud fraction.
w* — convective velocity scale; higher = stronger thermals (ft/min).
Cloud Cover — max cloud fraction over the column (0–100%).
Wind thresholds: orange = 12 mph, red = 18 mph.
